I looked over the PDF.

The one thing you do need to spell out is how
you randomly generate momenta at the start of
each iteration -- that wasn't clear to me from the
writeup.

Because you're going to be estimating the covariance
at exponentially increasing sizes, the matrix ops
only get executed around log2(N/10) times where
N is the number of warmup iterations.

Is the Cholesky factorization more stable than
inversion? Is it straightforward to estimate a
precision matrix instead of a covariance matrix?

Radford's paper doesn't push the equations for
a mass matrix through the leapfrog, and I don't
trust myself even to verify you've done the algebra
right. It looks OK to me, but could someone else check
it? The alternative is to implement the standard
way and your way and make sure they give you the same
answers.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: nondiag leapfrog in HMC
parts:
On Saturday, November 17, 2012 4:23:43 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Is the Cholesky factorization more stable than
inversion?

Somewhat. Essentially all inversion subroutines for positive definite matrices do a Cholesky factorization, an inversion of the Cholesky factor, and a product of the inverse Cholesky factor with its transpose. So, inversion somewhat exacerbates whatever imprecision there is, but the main thing is that inversion has two extra steps.

Eigen has a LDL' decomposition that is faster and more precise that the LL' decomposition (because the latter requires sqrts). However, the LDL' decomposition does pivoting (which helps avoid precision loss) so the decomposition is actually PLDL'P' where P is a permutation matrix. So, if we were to go that route, we need to incorporate the P matrix (not that difficult and Eigen optimizes that product).

Is it straightforward to estimate a
precision matrix instead of a covariance matrix?
Not from "data".

Radford's paper doesn't push the equations for
a mass matrix through the leapfrog, and I don't
trust myself even to verify you've done the algebra
right.  It looks OK to me, but could someone else check
it?  The alternative is to implement the standard
way and your way and make sure they give you the same
answers.

It looks okay to me. I actually put something analogous into the reparameterization subsection of the Stan manual a few days ago.

Ben

Yeah, sorry, I was focusing on the evolution and not on the entire algorithm. It's really the equation directly above (1) -- pi(p | q) = N(p | 0, M). When you resample the momenta you're sampling from the conditional distribution pi(p | q). When you have a non-trivial mass matrix you have to take that into account when resampling. This should already have been implemented for NUTS II as the sampled momenta will have different variances...

> I meant something in algorithmic form. You provided
> some equations, but I wasn't confident about how to
> tie that back to the full HMC algorithm.

Yuanjun's derivation looks good to me -- all he's doing is redefining the momenta in the integrator.  It's basically the same transformation that you guys use right now to yield "different stepsizes for each variable".
